The app itself is fine but does pretty much what a pen and paper can do. I imagine it will be necessary for some.

The community though really needs some severe moderation, unfortunately the so called mods join in with the banter and it just feels like an anxiety fuelled crèche with little direction.

If you want a basic goal tracker with some basic breathing exercises and some easily googleable articles thrown in then go ahead and spend £20 here. Otherwise there’s better “science backed” options out there. Disappointed.

The app has a lot of great ideas and features. Namely, it’s user friendly, the user interface is efficient and compact with a lot of different features. The overall design quality of the app is of a high standard which makes the price feel very reasonable. I personally think the leaderboard, and post areas are a great addition which encourage users to persist in their goals. 

The only real issue I have is functionality. First time I used the app, the internet filter didn’t work at all despite following the steps to activate it. I had to redownload the app to get it to work, and by doing so, I lost all the data I put into the app; journal entries, reasons to quit, my posts. My streak.

 I can look past this, but it is frustrating and unfortunate. Additionally, there’s an option to edit how long you’ve been abstaining for which even after redownloading still doesn’t work on my phone so my streak is now inaccurate. I also noticed that when reading community posts in the app, I was able to upvote a post multiple times which I assumed was a bug as that would portray an inaccurate number of times a post has been upvoted by different users.

Overall, I would recommend this app. It has a great purpose which has been executed well with a few practical resources that make it feel like a proactive journey in the app. There are functionality issues which compromise the usage of the app, but I could foresee these easily being ironed out, and as much as they’re not ideal, they don’t make it a deal breaker for the app.
